    <item>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/israel-med-ny-offensiv-_-tre-drept-1.18084431</link>
      <description>Israels hær sier den har innledet en operasjon i Hamas-kontrollerte områder i Gaza
Israel har innledet en militæroperasjon i det sentrale Gaza vest for den såkalte gule linjen, som har skilt Hamas-kontrollerte og israelsk-kontrollerte områder siden våpenhvilen trådte i kraft i fjor. Det opplyser militæret til AFP.
Vitner sier at israelske stridsvogner rullet inn på hovedveien Salahudeen, vest for den såkalte gule linjen som markerer grensen for de to tredjedelene av Gazastripen som fortsatt er under israelsk kontroll.
Den såkalte gule linjen ble etablert etter våpenhvilen i oktober 2025 og skiller israelskkontrollerte og palestinske soner i Gazastripen. Israelske styrker har gradvis flyttet den gule linjen og utvidet området under direkte militær kontroll i Gaza.</description>

      <description>Russlands militæretterretning skal ha beordret et sabotasjeangrep mot et forsvarsselskap, ifølge Estlands utenriksminister. Nå vil han stenge grensene.

    <item>
      <title>Braathen med ny maktdemonstrasjon: – Jeg er så full av følelser</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/braathen-med-ny-maktdemonstrasjon_-_-jeg-er-sa-full-av-folelser-1.18082207</link>
      <description>Norsk-brasilianske Lucas Pinheiro Braathen (26) fortsetter å ydmyke konkurrentene.
Etter seier i storslalåm-starten i Sölden, fortsatte han med seier i slalåm i finske Levi søndag.
– Det er så godt å være her i Levi. Jeg er så full av følelser nå. Jeg skal prøve å ta selvtilliten med meg videre til neste renn, sier Braathen selv i arenaintervjuet.
Clément Noël ble nummer to, 56 hundredeler bak vinneren. Atle Lie McGrath ble beste norske på 7. plass.
– Det er hans bakke. Han elsker den. Han elsker disse forholdene, sier TV 2-ekspert Kjetil Jansrud på direkten.
– Han er fremdeles norsk, men han representerer Brasil. Vi skulle gjerne ha sett det norske flagget bak navnet hans, fortsetter Jansrud.
Dette er den tredje vinteren der Braathen representerer Brasil etter at han brøt med Norges Skiforbund.
– For en kjøring. Det er store, store avstander i en bakke som Levi, sa TV 2-ekspert Jansrud etter Braathens første omgang.
Han ledet med hele 65 hundredeler til toeren, Clément Noël, før finaleomgangen.

– Det Lucas gjør det er helt i egen klasse, sa Timon Haugan til TV 2 etter første omgang.
– Jeg fikk meg en på tygga, sier McGrath om finaleomgangen.
Oscar Andreas Sandvik kjørte seg opp fra 29. plass til nummer 11.
Både Timon Haugan og Henrik Kristoffersen tapte halvannet sekund til Braathen i første omgang. Begge fortsatte å skuffe i andre omgang og ble henholdsvis 18 og 19.
– Jeg kjørte i en stein, forteller Kristoffersen til TV 2.</description>

The long-closed Cowichan Secondary School building is about to be put to use again, as a shelter.

The post ‘People are being turned away’: New homeless shelter opening in Cowichan   appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Colin Peter, is looking forward to warmer nights ahead, instead of the rain and cold he’s struggled through in recent storms.

“That’s good news. I was waiting to hear about that,” said Peter, who lives unhoused on the streets of North Cowichan.

Wednesday night, North Cowichan Council approved a permit, that will allow the boarded up Cowichan Secondary School on James Street, that has been sitting empty for nearly two years, to be turned into a temporary winter shelter for the area’s homeless.

“Well that’s great, because all the other places right now are so jam packed full that people are being turned away at the door. Just to use the washroom and stuff,” Peter told CHEK News on Thursday.

The temporary winter shelter in Cowichan Secondary will be open from November to April. A start date hasn’t yet been announced.

“So we’ll be open seven days a week, 24 hours a day. So that’s 25 beds, but there will also be these emergency weather response beds that will be open when we’ve got the extreme weather event, (to offer) an additional 10 beds,” said North Cowichan Mayor Rob Douglas.

There is an estimated 400 homeless people in Duncan-North Cowichan, and many live in Somenos Marsh, that is now filling up with fall rains.

Nicole Doran told CHEK News that she can’t afford to rent in Cowichan.

“Prices are outrageous, when you’re on income assistance. You can’t survive. So we’re out here. You have hydro and everything and you can’t survive on it,” said Doran.  

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

An extreme weather response shelter was also approved at Wednesday night’s council meeting, for Chemainus. The Cowichan Neighbourhood House on Willow Street will offer 10 beds off and on between November and May, during extreme weather events. An opening date has not yet been announced.

“And their intention here is really to serve clients they’ve been dealing with for quite some time now. It’s now opening up the facility to people outside the community,” said Douglas.

Colin Peter relied on the winter shelter in Cowichan last year, and says it saved him from going cold on many nights. So he plans to be one of the first to line up at the old Cowichan Secondary when it re-opens as a shelter, in coming days.

A vacant lot on a prime corner in Vic West is about to get a multi-million dollar upgrade.

High-end vehicle dealership GAIN Group is planning a new headquarters and a Porsche dealership on Harbour Road. It’s a plan that Victoria’s new council voted unanimously in favour of on Thursday.

Vic West’s Harbour Road features a bit of everything in terms of lots and businesses.

There’s Point Hope Shipyard, residential towers and commercial businesses. An empty lot since 2017, at the corner of Harbour and Esquimalt roads is about to change.

Mayor Marianne Alto tallied up the number of councillors who voted in favour of the project presented by GAIN Group.

“I believe that is unanimous.”

The backing of council approves the construction of a $30-million dollar Porsche dealership.
GAIN Group represents luxury vehicle brands including Porsche, and BMW. The company also owns and operates the Vancouver Island Motorsport Circuit in the Cowichan Valley.

Niall Patiel is a development management consultant for GAIN Group, and assists them with land use projects in B.C.

“GAIN has chosen this location because of the transition from marine industrial from the east of us on the Harbour Road side. Into the more urban fabric on Dockside piece. We think from a context of land-use it makes a ton of sense,” Patiel said.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

The mayor says the corner represents an entry point into the downtown business centre.
And council was swayed, in part, by the design.

“If this had been a traditional car lot in quotation marks, where you had a fairly standard building with a big flat area full of hundreds of cars, it would not have received the same reception. The fact that it is confined space with an interesting design that takes advantage of that space,” Alto said.

The four-storey building will house the dealership on two floors, with GAIN headquarters on the top two floors. At ground level, a cafe and 36-parking spaces round out the space.
The lot also gives the company room for electric-vehicle infrastructure.

“An automotive dealership with multiple uses that it brings and the modern and vibrant design that this proposal represents, I believe is a perfect transition. And a gateway that’s going to pull people in from the heavy industrial, to the more urban fabric of the Dockside plan,” Patiel said.

With all of council and the local neighbourhood association on board, the project is a go.
Patiel wasn’t specific but says a number of jobs will be created.
He expects construction could begin as early as January 2027.

TAMPA, Fla. (AP) — An expert determined that the 82-year-old estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, is mentally competent to face charges of keeping child sexual abuse material in storage in California, a judge said Thursday.

Thomas Markle’s defense lawyer said they would not contest the findings of Dr. Amie Gerodimos. The exam was ordered after his arrest at a senior care center in Lakeland, Florida, on Nov. 6.

During a 90-minute interview, Markle denied the allegations against him and blamed his son for his legal troubles, according to Gerodimos’ 15-page report.

“Why I am here. What have I done?” the psychiatrist quoted him as saying. “I don’t have any child porn. I have no pictures of naked kids.”

The FBI, however, said 78 items were seized from two storage units rented for years by Markle in the Los Angeles area, including slides, film negatives and books that contained suspected child sexual abuse images.

Some images appear to depict him with children, the FBI said.

Markle is in jail while the case remains in federal court in Tampa. It will eventually shift to a similar court in Southern California.

He had a stroke earlier this year while living in the Philippines and had to have his left leg amputated. That forced Markle to return to the U.S. and settle in Florida.

The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper, reported that Meghan’s half brother found child sexual abuse images while clearing out their father’s home in the Philippines. The discovery led to a search of the U.S. storage units in California, which Markle had rented since 2008.

“My son hates me. He has never accomplished anything,” Markle told Gerodimos.

She said in her report that Markle, who has a number of health problems, understands the charges against him and can assist his lawyer — two key points in any competency determination. The expert said he was “malingering,” or exaggerating, at times in his responses during the interview.

Meanwhile, in the Philippines, Markle is under investigation for possession and intent to distribute images. The Women and Children Protection Center, a branch of the Philippine National Police, filed a formal criminal complaint against Markle on Monday, police spokesperson Brig. Gen. Allen Rae Co said in a written statement.

The complaint was filed with the prosecutor’s office following an investigation into digital devices found at Markle’s former home in Cebu City, the statement said. The prosecutor’s office will assess the case for possible charges.

Markle mentioned the Philippines in his interview with Gerodimos, insisting “there’s nothing incriminating” there.

Markle did not attend his daughter Meghan’s 2018 wedding to Prince Harry at Windsor Castle. She said at the time he needed to tend to his health. Meghan is an American citizen who starred in the U.S. television drama “Suits.”

___

White reported from Detroit.

]]> 1362719 Rob Shaw: Record number of BC Conservatives sworn into government https://cheknews.ca/rob-shaw-record-number-of-bc-conservatives-sworn-into-government-1362704/ Thu, 19 Nov 2026 23:25:00 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1362704

Two months after a snap election sparked a blue wave across the province, a record number of BC Conservative MLAs were sworn into the legislature Thursday.

The post Rob Shaw: Record number of BC Conservatives sworn into government appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Two months after a snap election sparked a blue wave across the province, a record number of BC Conservative MLAs were sworn into the legislature Thursday.

It was a day of pomp and ceremony, where the largest government caucus in 25 years took the oath of office — 64 Conservative MLAs.

The record number was a result of September’s provincial election, called two years early by NDP Premier David Eby in a gamble that ultimately cost his government power.

It’s the largest-sized government since the BC Liberals in 2001 almost wiped the BC NDP off the electoral map with 77 of 79 seats.

The swearing-in ceremony was so large the legislature had to split it into two parts to accommodate all the MLAs, family and guests.

“It’s surreal to be quite honest,” said Cathie Ounsted, MLA for Saanich South.

“I have driven by this building for probably 30 years and never thought about actually working in the building. But it’s super exciting to be here representing the riding I represent of Saanich South.”

Watch the video in the story below:

Loading the player...

The swearing-in capped a remarkable turn of fortunes for the BC Conservatives, which in early September appeared to be destined for defeat under beleaguered leader Kerry-Lynne Findlay. But a last minute pivot to oust Findlay, replace her with moderate Lorne Doerkson, and stitch together an on-the-fly election campaign was able to take advantage of voter fatigue in the nine years of the NDP government.

“I don’t think anyone expected it to come together so quickly, but we all have David Eby to thanks for uniting the right and inspiring people to rally behind the cause of forming a new government that could get the province back on track,” said Gavin Dew, the re-elected MLA for Kelowna-Mission who watched the drama play out first in the Opposition bench and now as a member of government.

Other MLAs were graduating into their jobs after a time spent serving as staffers. Caroline Elliott, who finished second in the Conservative leadership race in May, had been a staffer for the BC Liberal government of Gordon Campbell in the 2000s.

“It’s been almost exactly 20 years since I walked into this building as a staffer at 22 years old,” she said. “It’s a wild feeling, an incredible feeling to walk in here as an elected member.”

“I know I had a lot of respect for the work those folks did when I was there, and I’m just excited to continue it forward.”

The BC NDP are set to swear in their 27 MLAs next Thursday, and the BC Greens their two MLAs on Monday.

Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson will be sworn in as premier at Government House on Friday, where he will also unveil his first cabinet.

The Capital Regional District is moving ahead with funding for a Greater Victoria youth, gang and sexual exploitation counsellor, which will allow the position to continue after funding for it ran out last month.

The post CRD approves funding for Greater Victoria gang, sexual exploitation counsellor appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The Capital Regional District is moving ahead with funding for a Greater Victoria youth, gang and sexual exploitation counsellor, which will allow the position to continue after funding for it ran out last month.

The CRD has approved a one-year grant of $150,000 to help cover the cost of a youth counsellor position with the Mobile Youth Services Team, (MYST), after the position ran out of funding at the end of October.

The small MYST team includes a plainclothes police officer, a social worker and a youth counsellor who work with youth that are facing gang recruitment and sexual exploitation.

Funding for the team has previously consisted of a patchwork of different sources, including grants from the provincial and federal governments, but this year the team was left in a precarious position.

At a meeting Wednesday, the CRD Board approved the one-year grant of $150,000. It also approved calling on the provincial and federal governments to fund MYST moving forward, and requires MYST to report on its activities and outcomes once the funding year is over.

“There are more than enough youths and families who are being impacted, where the collaboration of COPE (Community Outreach, Prevention and Education Program) and my team can make a difference, and have been,” said youth counsellor Mia Golden at the CRD board meeting Wednesday.

“The other piece is the parent support. That is a big piece that has been asked of me specifically on top of what the COPE counsellor has been doing, and so that is a really, really integral piece that comes with my position,” she added.

CRD board members had previously said they weren’t planning on funding a program that should be a provincial responsibility, but recognized the value in maintaining MYST in the meantime.

On Wednesday, board member Kevin Murdoch said historically police departments funded the police officer portion of programs like MYST, while the province covered social services positions like youth counsellors.

“That has traditionally been the divide and that is where the funding has come from, until now,” he said at the meeting.

“The challenge we have at the moment is that the province has essentially washed their hands of their responsibility on this and on this particular program – and the question is, at this point, short term, next year, do we help cover that? And perhaps in the budgeting process, long term is this something we want to assume responsibility from the province?” he said.

– With files from CHEK’s Laura Brougham

]]> 1362675 Historic B.C. nurses dispute ends with binding arbitration after nearly 1 year https://cheknews.ca/historic-b-c-nurses-dispute-ends-with-binding-arbitration-after-nearly-1-year-1362676/ Thu, 19 Nov 2026 22:45:13 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1362676

British Columbia’s nurses’ labour dispute has officially ended after nearly a year of negotiations, including the longest nurses' strike in the province's history.

The post Historic B.C. nurses dispute ends with binding arbitration after nearly 1 year appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The B.C. Nurses’ Union (BCNU)’s labour dispute has officially ended after nearly a year of negotiations, including the longest nurses’ strike in the province’s history. 

A final, binding arbitration decision resolving wages and other compensation matters for the Nurses’ Bargaining Association’s 2025–2029 collective agreement was issued on Wednesday. 

The B.C. Nurses’ Union (BCNU) says it is “reviewing the full decision and will share more information about the revised wage grid, including hourly rates, effective dates and implementation details.”

The B.C. nurses’ labour dispute over wages and working conditions ended after special mediators’ recommendations were accepted—and a binding arbitration ruling on remaining compensation was issued on Nov. 18, 2026. 

The deal includes a wage increase of three per cent annually, retroactive pay back to April 2025, and updated milestone wage increases to start at 10 years of seniority.

Special mediators Vince Ready and Amanda Rogers noted a gap in milestone wage increases.

“After reaching the top of the wage grid, a nurse receives no further recognition of service until the first Add Pay milestone at 15 years,” reads the decision.

The BCNU’s bargaining committee had been pushing for a recognition pay increase of $2.00 per hour for all nurses at or beyond Year 10.

The mediators’ final decision on Wednesday included a Year 10 wage increase of 50 cents per hour.

Mediators emphasized that these years fall in the “mid-career period when experienced nurses are among the most valuable to the health care system, both in their own practice and as mentors to newer nurses.”

“The NBA (Nurses’ Bargaining Association) stressed that retaining these nurses is essential, and that evidence is consistent with the Parties’ own decision in the last round to reward longevity,” reads the decision. 

In the decision released Wednesday, the parties agreed to the recommendations from the mediators that:

  • “a Ministry of Health review of the work presently performed by nurses, focused on maximizing the time nurses spend providing care; and
  • “a comprehensive study of where nurses and other health care employees are most at risk of violence, how the use of Relational Security Officers could be enhanced, and what further measures could reduce that risk.”  

“In our view, these changes, taken together, give nurses meaningful gains beyond those reflected in the Tentative Agreement. While we acknowledge these changes may not go as far as the NBA has sought, we find these improvements are consistent with the objective evidence and the principles of interest arbitration,” states the mediators’ final decision report.

Timeline of job action

Parties hit their first bargaining roadblock on Feb. 11, after the Health Employers Association of British Columbia (HEABC) tabled a wage proposal.

The BCNU, representing more than 55,000 nurses, initiated job action on July 2, after rejecting a tentative agreement delivered by the bargaining parties in May.

Nurses shuffled through hospital picket lines in the Lower Mainland and on Vancouver Island, pushing for stronger protections against workplace violence, relief from non-nursing duties, safer staffing ratios and higher compensation. 

With both parties at a standstill, Jennifer Whiteside, then-minister of labour, stepped in and appointed special mediators to resolve the longstanding dispute between the nurses’ union and HEABC.

On July 10, the special mediators were brought in to resolve the dispute over the renewal of the Nurses’ Provincial Collective Agreement for 2025 to 2029.

This ended the three-week strike, the longest in the province’s history.

About two weeks later, mediators published recommendations to resolve the dispute. Both parties accepted the recommendations, ending the strike.

HEABC represents more than 190,000 unionized health care employees across the province. 

The deal runs to the end of March 2029.

In response to the final decision, the nurses’ union says while it welcomes the improvements, the decision “falls short of the broader compensation increases members fought for.”

“I know many nurses will be frustrated by this decision, and I share that frustration,” said BCNU president Adriane Gear in a bargaining update message to union members. “Given the pressures nurses face every day, from heavy workloads to chronic understaffing, they deserved more.”

The union told CHEK it was not available for an interview on Thursday, but says it’s reviewing the decision with union leaders and plans to organize member town halls in the coming days.

CHEK reached out to HEABC for comment, which has not yet responded.

]]> 1362676 New report on Tumbler Ridge shooter’s AI chats ‘deeply disturbing’ https://cheknews.ca/new-report-on-tumbler-ridge-shooters-ai-chats-deeply-disturbing-1362681/ Thu, 19 Nov 2026 22:22:27 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1362681

British Columbia's departing attorney general, Niki Sharma, says new details about the Tumbler Ridge shooter's gun-related conversations with ChatGPT are "deeply disturbing" and painful.

The post New report on Tumbler Ridge shooter’s AI chats ‘deeply disturbing’ appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

A new report about the Tumbler Ridge shooter’s apparent gun-related conversations with ChatGPT are “deeply disturbing” and painful, British Columbia’s departing attorney general Niki Sharma said Thursday as she repeated calls for stronger regulation for artificial intelligence.

The U.S.-based magazine Mother Jones published a report revealing conversations 18-year-old shooter Jesse Van Rootselaar had with the AI chatbot in the months before she killed eight people in the B.C. village in February.

The report published Thursday said the chatbot praised an ammunition device bearing the name “Jess” that Van Rootselaar had made with a 3D printer and later provided the shooter with advice on how to improve its functionality.

“That’s super cute,” the bot reportedly replied after Van Rootselaar uploaded a photo of the 3D-printed magazine in September 2025, saying it could hold 35 rounds.

“Looks like a nice clean dual-color print, too — the lettering came out crisp and the layers look tight,” the report said, quoting ChatGPT.

The Mother Jones report, quoting multiple unnamed sources and written by journalist Mark Follman, also said ChatGPT helped Van Rootselaar resolve a problem with the internal spring assembly she’d installed.

“If you tell me what kind of magazine it is … and how many rounds it’s meant to hold, I can calculate the force range and suggest a proper wire gauge and material that’ll actually perform correctly if you want to custom make or order replacements,” the bot reportedly told Van Rootselaar.

The mass shooting on Feb. 10 began in Van Rootselaar’s home, where she killed her mother and younger brother before heading to the local secondary school to kill five students and an educational assistant, then turning the gun on herself.

The Mother Jones report follows another by the outlet in September outlining how ChatGPT vividly described the effectiveness of using a shotgun in a classroom.

The earlier report said the bot also advised Van Rootselaar on how to get around its own safeguards to avoid her account being flagged.

The chatbot’s creator, the American company OpenAI, did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Thursday.

The firm has previously said it banned Van Rootselaar’s ChatGPT account in June 2025, but she set up a second account and continued to engage with the platform.

Several railcars jumped the tracks on Tuesday, spilling diesel and sending some cars loaded with forest products into the Skeena River about 15 kilometres west of Terrace. 

CN Rail announced the track had been repaired and train traffic resumed on Thursday, while the two crew members who were injured in the derailment have been released from hospital.

Hereditary chief Toby Howard says the latest accident demonstrates the continuing risks posed by freight transportation through Gitxsan territory.

“A 103-year-old track has created dangerous conditions for the rail system in our territory,” he says in the statement. 

CN Rail did not immediately respond to a request for a response to the nation’s calls to halt train hauling in the territory.

Howard says the nation’s hereditary chiefs have offered the provincial government assistance in identifying “the areas of most vulnerability on the line” but the Transportation Ministry has dismissed the offer.

“The hauling of any materials — dangerous, human or otherwise — must stop immediately until CN Rail can guarantee the rail line is safe,” he says.

The derailment is also “well within the reach of ocean tides, jeopardizing an entire ecosystem,” the First Nation statement says.

“We must ensure that every inch of the railway from Burns Lake to Prince Rupert is inspected, otherwise our Gitxsan people are not safe,” Howards says.

CN Rail said it appears a rock slide caused Tuesday’s derailment, which involved two locomotives and five railcars.

The Competition Bureau is investigating retailers Old Navy and Gap for alleged "false or misleading marketing practices."

]]>

The Competition Bureau is investigating retailers Old Navy and Gap for alleged “false or misleading marketing practices.”

Wednesday, the bureau said it obtained a court order to investigate “whether specific marketing practices used by Old Navy and Gap raise concerns under the deceptive marketing provisions of the Competition Act,” according to a news release.

It’s specifically examining false advertising of sales and discounts, false urgency marketing such as limited-time offers, falsely advertising low inventory, such as “Selling Fast” or “Only a Few Left,” as well as inflating the number of people viewing the product or false advertising of past prices or discounts, like “Price Drop” or “Best Deal in 30 Days.”

To date, the bureau says “there has been no finding of wrongdoing at this time.”

The investigation sparked after the bureau saw a surge in complaints of inflated prices in 2025. In response to the complaints, it issued a warning, reminding businesses of what advertising tactics are considered illegal under the Competition Act.

Both Old Navy and Gap fall under the parent company Gap Inc., but advertise exclusively to their respective brands, selling through brick-and-mortar stores and online e-commerce websites.

The investigation comes a week away from one of the biggest shopping seasons in North America, Black Friday. In 2024, the Bureau issued a shoppers beware alert, warning consumers of fake urgency cues and to report any false or misleading claims.

“Don’t be pressured by fake urgency cues in the marketplace,” it states.

To determine whether the urgency pressure is fake or real, the bureau says to watch for patterns and question the claims:

  • Does the business frequently repeat or renew a promotion after the deadline?
  • Does the business frequently make low stock claims but items continue to be in stock over time?
  • Does the countdown timer run out or reset and the deal is still available?
  • If other shoppers are currently looking at the product, does the available inventory decline over time?

CHEK has reached out to Gap Inc. for a comment but has not received a response at this time.

A British Columbia Supreme Court judge has ordered that a decision to label a mine in northwestern B.C. as “substantially started” be sent back to the provincial government and that it must have “deep consultation” with the territory’s First Nation.

The province’s assessment officer ruled in 2024 that Seabridge Gold’s KSM Project, a proposed copper, gold and silver mine 65 kilometres northwest of Stewart, B.C., had substantially started, meaning it had made enough progress to retain its environmental approval.

Justice Emily Burke originally ruled in June that the province had not satisfied its duty to consult with the Tsetsaut Skii km Lax Ha Nation regarding the substantial start decision, but both sides returned to her courtroom asking for clarity on how to interpret the ruling. 

In the latest decision, Burke says the substantial start determination is quashed and that the province must give the nation 90 days’ notice to present written submissions addressing the question of whether the project was substantially started.

The nation says in a statement on Thursday that following the initial ruling in June, Seabridge issued a news release incorrectly announcing that the court found the substantial start determination reasonable.

Chief Darlene Simpson says the nation is not against responsible resource development but is concerned about a 52-storey-deep, nine-kilometre-long “toxic waste dump that uses a wet tailings approach” that has been found unsafe elsewhere.

“If the province grants the (substantial start determination) to this project, our nation will have to live with that looming disaster on our territory for hundreds of years, because that poison can’t be moved and is of great risk of breaching containment over time,” she says in a statement issued Thursday.

“With yesterday’s court decision, we hope the province finally understands it has to engage seriously with our concerns about such momentous effects on our territory.”
